author: Shi Jiangtao
description:
Beijing is doubling down on overland trade routes across Central Asia as continued disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz and the wider region expose the vulnerability of global shipping chokepoints.
A new link to Afghanistan via Uzbekistan offers a practical example of this long-term diversification push. However, observers caution that security concerns and capacity constraints could make a meaningful shift away from sea freight difficult.
Officially launched in May with pilot shipments, the...
title: Amid Hormuz woes, China tests Central Asian land corridors to bypass maritime chokepoints

author: Vincent Chow
description:
A group of American tech giants, including Nvidia, Palantir and Meta, signed a public letter on Friday calling for US leadership in open-weight AI models, an area that China currently dominates.
The challenge comes amid growing speculation that the Trump administration might introduce restrictions on open AI models.
These would aim to address national security risks of the fast-moving technology and combat the growing popularity of Chinese models, a move that critics say would instead hurt US...
title: Nvidia, Palantir, Meta warn against ‘premature restrictions’ of open-weight models

author: Han Li
description:
Washington and Beijing’s top police officials met on Friday in the Chinese capital, the latest meeting by senior level representatives in advance of a much-anticipated summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, expected in the US capital in late September.
Federal Bureau of Investigation Director Kash Patel met Wang Xiaohong, China’s state councillor and minister of public security, in Beijing on Friday, according to state news agency Xinhua.
Wang said the two...
title: FBI director meets China’s public security chief in Beijing on crime crackdown

author: Carol Yang,Fan Chen
description:
Washington’s recent wave of trade, tech and visa restrictions on China appears to be a deliberate push to build leverage ahead of the presidential summit in September, according to Chinese analysts.
However, they warn that such aggressive pressure tactics risk souring the political atmosphere ahead of the high-stakes meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping.
The assessment comes as the two powers seek to establish a new framework of “constructive strategic stability”, in line with the...
title: Will Donald Trump’s China squeeze for summit leverage actually work?

author: Zhang Tong
description:
Two Peking University alumni made history by winning the Fields Medal this week, a victory that points to a wave of young, high-achieving Chinese scientists behind them.
The International Congress of Mathematicians announced that Wang Hong and Deng Yu, who both entered the top Chinese university in 2007, were awarded the highest honour for mathematicians under 40 years of age.
It is the first time Chinese nationals have received the prestigious award.
Mathematician Cai Tianxin, a distinguished...
title: Fields Medallists highlight new wave of Chinese scientists leading global research

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
China may be developing a new class of nuclear-powered attack submarine with improved range and stealth, according to analysis based on recent satellite imagery.
The images, captured at Shanghai’s Jiangnan Shipyard, show what analysts believe is a previously unidentified submarine featuring a dramatically reduced sail compared with existing Type 093 attack submarines – a design they say could improve performance.
The submarine first came to public attention in early June when naval analyst H.I....
title: Is China building a new type of attack submarine? Satellite images hint at stealth gains

author: Shi Jiangtao
description:
The Association of Southeast Asian Nations and China have called for a lasting settlement to the current war in the Middle East and pledged further cooperation on energy security.
A joint statement, released after a meeting between the bloc’s foreign ministers and their Chinese counterpart in Manila, came amid an ongoing energy crisis.
The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has caused prices to rise and led to shortages across Southeast Asia, prompting the Philippines to declare a national energy...
title: China and Asean eye closer energy cooperation as fighting flares up again in Middle East

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
In an era where short-form videos and viral commentary can dominate public discourse on geopolitics, one Chinese political scientist is on a mission to correct what he calls a “negative one” level of understanding.
Yan Xuetong, honorary president of Tsinghua University’s Institute of International Relations in Beijing, is doing this by challenging the public to avoid social media sensationalism and to take a 60-minute closed-book test on their grasp of foreign affairs.
The fourth edition of the...
title: Why a Chinese political scientist wants the public to take a test on foreign affairs

author: David Dodwell
description:
After devoting the first half of 2026 to an ineffectual, expensive and inconclusive military adventure in Iran, it seems US President Donald Trump is about to turn afresh to the wars he loves best – the tariff wars he still believes can make America great again.
He can’t quite walk away from the war in the Persian Gulf. Iran’s refusal to capitulate has left Trump with an awkward obligation to fight on, despite the widespread unpopularity of the conflict, even among his base, and the need to...
title: Trump’s latest tariff tantrum unlikely to end well for the US

author: Liu Zhen
description:
South Korea has returned a pair of Qing dynasty (1644-1911) marble sculptures to China, a symbolic gesture as the two nations work to repair bilateral ties through cultural diplomacy.
The male and female lions, each standing 1.9 metres (6ft) tall and weighing 1.25 tonnes, were officially handed over by the Kansong Art Museum at a ceremony in Seoul on Thursday and were set to depart for China on Friday, according to the Chinese embassy.
Senior cultural officials and diplomats from both nations...
title: South Korea returns looted Qing dynasty lions to China in cultural diplomacy win

author: Orange Wang
description:
China-Philippine clashes continued near the hotly contested Scarborough Shoal for the second day on Friday, as Beijing started military drills in the South China Sea that are expected to run until the end of the month.
“On July 24, the China Coast Guard took control measures in accordance with the law toward multiple Philippine vessels engaged in illegal activities in waters under China’s jurisdiction off Huangyan Island,” the coastguard said in a statement on Friday, referring to Beijing’s name...
title: South China Sea: Beijing and Manila trade blame on second day of Scarborough Shoal clashes

author: Chao Kong
description:
From massive typhoons and severe floods to scorching heat, China is being hit by a barrage of extreme weather events. Behind this surge in volatility lies a brewing “super” El Nino, according to researchers.
Scientists warn that we are only seeing the prelude, and with the current event already rivalling historic climate disasters, it signals a potentially perilous future for the nation and the globe.
Jiang Hua, chief El Nino forecaster at the National Marine Environmental Forecasting Centre,...
title: Super El Nino: is 2026 an ‘extremely destructive’ prelude? Next year might be worse

author: Haining Gao
description:
China unveiled its 15th five-year plan for renewable energy on Thursday. Below are the key targets outlined in the blueprint, which was released jointly by the National Development and Reform Commission and National Energy Administration.

可再生能源发展“十五五”规划 by scmp
title: China’s 15th five-year plan for renewable energy development

author: SCMP
description:
We have selected seven stories from this week’s news across Hong Kong, mainland China, the wider Asia region and beyond that resonated with our readers and shed light on topical issues. If you would like to see more of our reporting, please consider subscribing.
1. US slaps fresh tariffs on China, 50-plus countries in latest wave
The United States imposed late on Thursday a fresh wave of tariffs against 60 countries, including China, Japan, South Korea, India and European Union member states,...
title: Fresh US tariffs on 60 countries; first China duo win Fields Medal: SCMP’s 7 highlights

author: Shi Jiangtao
description:
Joseph Chang Yanfeng was ordained bishop of Chifeng in China’s northern Inner Mongolia autonomous region on Wednesday, highlighting the uneasy diplomatic engagement between Beijing and the Vatican on the sensitive issue of Catholic appointments.
According to Vatican News, Pope Leo XIV approved Chang’s appointment on June 15, under the terms of the 2018 provisional agreement between the Holy See and Beijing.
The ordination fills a vacancy for the Catholic diocese of Chifeng that had lasted nearly...
title: Vatican and Beijing agree on new China bishop as ordination fills 20-year vacancy

author: Kandy Wong
description:
Simon Johnson is a professor of entrepreneurship at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). A former chief economist of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), he won a joint Nobel Prize for economics in 2024 for his research into how institutions shape national prosperity. On June 8, the British government announced Johnson as chair of its new AI Economics Institute.
In this interview, conducted on the sidelines of the UBS Asian Investment Conference in Hong Kong, Johnson discussed the...
title: Nobel economist on anti-China, anti-science US, AI’s risks

author: Bernard Chan
description:
Officials talking about artificial intelligence (AI) often speak in terms of the next industrial revolution or existential risks. Such rhetoric ultimately does little to capture how AI filters into the ordinary workings of a city like Hong Kong.
The geopolitics of AI are no longer abstract. They are beginning to shape who can use which tools – and on what terms.
Over the past few months, two major international banks in the city have reportedly felt the impact. Anthropic’s Claude, a generative...
title: Hong Kong must wake up to the cold hard geopolitics of AI

author: Mark Magnier
description:
Two Chinese nationals pleaded guilty to shipping more than 500 turtles to Hong Kong in violation of American wildlife law, the US Department of Justice said on Thursday.
Kin Keung Ho pleaded guilty on Thursday while Lihua Owen Ma pleaded guilty to a similar charge on July 1. Both are residents of Staten Island, one of the five boroughs of New York City.
“During the plea hearing, the government proffered that Ho shipped approximately 99 packages containing 578 turtles,” the agency said. “Ho...
title: Chinese nationals plead guilty to illegally shipping turtles from US to Hong Kong

author: Ling Xin
description:
China has unveiled its latest ambitious space-based computing network designed to process satellite data in orbit using AI before sending the results to Earth.
Xingshu, or “Star Hub”, will eventually comprise around 1,000 satellites, according to Chi Nan, an optical communications professor at Fudan University.
The network is being jointly developed by Fudan and Shanghai Xingshu Tiansuan Space Technology Co.
It would offer on-demand, time-based computing services in orbit, allowing governments,...
title: China targets new space-based computing network to process data born in orbit
